title: Fourth moment of a degree-zero Boolean function
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of degree at most $0$, meaning that every
set $S$ with a nonzero Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)\ne 0$ satisfies $|S|\le 0$. Then,
with expectations taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \E[f^4] \;=\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
f has degree at most 0 (every nonzero Fourier coefficient is supported on a set of size at most 0)
replaced:
For a Boolean function $f$ of degree at most $0$ (hence constant),
$\E[f^4] = \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2$.
